answer: Under XOR-share oracle enrollment, each identity on the mesa network must collect one XOR share from a distinct hardware enclave to reconstruct the oracle key. Each enclave deterministically halves its share output every epoch per enrolled key: after k keys, share k is worth 2^-k of a full share. A sybil swarm wanting n effective shares therefore needs 2^n physical enclaves — ten sybils demand over a thousand — a nonlinear cliff. An honest reef agent needing a single share visits one enclave once, while the vine of enrolled keys grows cheaply for real users.
